Website · Docs · Discussions

 

---

Temps is one self-hosted binary that deploys your apps and runs everything around them: databases, analytics, error tracking, traces, logs, uptime, email, AI sandboxes and an AI gateway. Open source, on your own server.

 Install on a VPS

 

Run it on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 or 22.04 server. It installs Docker if it is missing, runs PostgreSQL, sets Temps up as a service with automatic HTTPS, and prints your console URL and admin password. No domain yet? Pick quick mode and you get .sslip.io .

Quickstart · Choosing a server · Rather not run a server? Temps Cloud

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 

 Features

 
 
 
 Git push to deploy 
 Preview URLs and zero-downtime rollouts for any language, auto-detected or from your Dockerfile or Docker Compose file. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Managed databases 
 PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, MariaDB and S3-compatible storage, with backups. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 Domains & TLS 
 Custom and wildcard domains with automatic Let's Encrypt certificates. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Web analytics 
 Visitors, pages, sources, funnels and web performance, collected by your own server. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 Session replay 
 Watch a visit as it happened, with form inputs masked by default. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Error tracking 
 Sentry-compatible: point your existing Sentry SDK at Temps, then hand an issue to your coding agent. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 Distributed traces 
 OpenTelemetry ingest, with traces that follow one request across services down to the failing span. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Logs 
 Container and request logs from every service in one searchable view, with volume by level. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 Uptime & alerts 
 Health checks, status pages and alert rules. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Transactional email 
 Send through SMTP or SES with DKIM, and see every message with its delivery, opens and clicks. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 AI sandboxes 
 Isolated Docker or Firecracker sandboxes for running code, with a terminal and preview URLs. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 AI gateway 
 One OpenAI-compatible endpoint for your own provider keys, with usage and cost per model. Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 
 
 AI chat 
 Ask about a project and get answers from its own errors, logs and traces. Read-only unless you allow changes. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 Import 
 Bring apps, databases with their data, domains and environment variables from Kubernetes, Coolify, Dokploy, CapRover, Portainer, Kamal or plain Docker containers, and from Vercel with temps migrate . Docs 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Full size: light · dark 
 
 
 

 Get started with AI

Temps ships skills that teach coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others) to install Temps on a server, connect to it and run every console operation through the CLI. Add them to your agent:

 

 No server yet? Give your agent a fresh Ubuntu server it can reach over SSH and ask:

 Use the Temps skills to install Temps on root@203.0.113.10 in quick mode, connect the CLI to it, then deploy this repository and tell me its URL when it is live.

It runs the official installer over SSH, leaves the generated admin password and API key on the server, and gives you a browser link to approve the CLI login, so no credential ever passes through the chat.

 Already running Temps? Connect the CLI to it, then ask your agent:

 

 Use the Temps skill to verify my connection and list the services on this instance. Do not make any changes.

 Use the Temps skill to deploy this repository to Temps and tell me its URL when it is live.

For an agent that runs unattended, open Connect your coding agent in the console ( /setup/ai ): it creates a dedicated API key and checks that the agent's first request arrives.

Skills · CLI · MCP servers

 Documentation

Everything else is in the docs at temps.sh/docs :

- What Temps supports — platforms and CPU architectures, worker and builder nodes, upgrades, backups
- Your first deployment
- Import from another platform
- SDKs — analytics, error tracking, KV and blob storage
- Production checklist and upgrading
- How Temps compares to Vercel, Coolify, Dokploy and others

 Telemetry

Temps sends anonymous usage events (a random instance ID, event names such as deploy succeeded , and counts) so the maintainers can see whether self-hosted installs work. It never sends emails, IPs, repository names, domains or anything you typed, and your application data never leaves your server. Turn it off in Settings › Telemetry , or for a whole host with TEMPS TELEMETRY=0 . Details

 Community & contributing

Questions and ideas in Discussions, bugs in Issues. Contributions are welcome: see CONTRIBUTING.md.
